chose: claim-record lookup identity is a branded ClaimKey minted only by claimKey(), with one exported map-mint (status.indexClaimRecords) that every reader of status.verify.claims goes through — merge, panel, verify's never-red filter, scene, promise
over: the one-line-per-site fix: call claimKey at the three raw-keyed sites and change nothing structural
persisting a key field on ClaimRecord in status.json
because: the one-line fix leaves raw keying representable, and this exact bug happened three times in parallel with the doc on claimKey already saying 'store AND read'; a persisted key field would be redundant data that can drift from node+claim and breaks old records. The brand makes a raw-string probe of an indexed map a compile error, and the single mint means a fourth consumer cannot quietly invent a fourth key regime (the merge had even drifted to a NUL separator)

chose: CI's verification step runs the FULL tier against the read-only snapshot, borrowing the workspace's node_modules via symlink
over: keeping verify --fast in CI and adding a separate full-tier job
running full verify in the workspace instead of the snapshot
because: audit M4 proved a retitled guard oracle leaves npm test and verify --fast green — only full verify reds it, so fast-in-CI is the hole itself, and a second job would double checkout/install for nothing at ~90s serial cost. The snapshot stays: it proves the committed tree verifies without generated artifacts; the symlink exists because guard-oracle test files resolve imports from the snapshot cwd and a bare archive has no deps (measured: 3 file-level import failures without it)

chose: node --test with a --test-name-pattern that matches NOTHING (single file) exits 0 AND reports 'tests 1 · pass 1' on node v25.2.1 — so the repo's testMatch 'pass [1-9]' is satisfiable by a run that ran no test
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
the file itself counts as one passing top-level test in newer node, making count-based positive evidence vacuous on this runner class
discriminatedBy: run the same zero-match pattern against a one-file suite and diff the summary against a one-match run: identical counts, and the only stable discriminator is the executed title echoed by the reporter

chose: the file counts as one passing test — count/exit evidence is vacuous on this runner; title-echo is the discriminator
because: ran both experiments: zero-match ('this matches nothing at all' over test/status.test.ts) and one-match ('merge — a fail replaces a pass') print IDENTICAL summaries (tests 1 · pass 1, exit 0); the one-match run alone carries the '✔ <title>' line. runNamedTest now requires the literal title echoed in a passing owner's output, and the contract test 'a title that survives only as a STRING fails' pins it

chose: the serial canary probes the exact claim path (runSerialNamedTest, factored from execNamedTest) once per verify at every serial grant — explicit opt-in AND batch fallback — and a passing canary is a refusal (refused=true), not a warning
over: canary as a warning line that lets the run stay green
probing only the explicit --serial-oracles path and trusting the fallback
because: a warning is exactly the silent-degrade shape v0.17 removed from the batch path, and the fallback is the serial route nobody typed — the one most in need of the proof; probing the shared serial arm means the canary cannot drift from what a real claim experiences

chose: run-named-test's logic moved into src/run-named-test.ts behind a two-line scripts/.mjs entry, and green now requires the executed title echoed in the run output
over: keeping the logic in scripts/ and adding only a contract test
counting '# tests N' from the child summary as positive evidence
because: sources:['src'] is the evidence perimeter — a contract test alone leaves the runner unclaimable by any boundary; and count-based evidence is vacuous on node v25 (d-09f93a9d: a zero-match run reports tests 1 · pass 1), while the reporter echoing the executed title survives reporter and version changes

chose: claim 1 anchors at execNamedTest, now exported — the seam-honest anchor — rather than at runVerify
over: anchoring at runVerify to avoid exporting a private function
because: the property lives at the single front door every runner invocation passes through; anchoring it two layers up would survive a refactor that bypasses the door, which is the exact orphaning class this batch of claims exists to catch. Exporting it also lets the graph see the seam
